newsitem.title: UK: UK-US open skies talks delayed for two weeks.
newsitem.headline: UK-US open skies talks delayed for two weeks.

text.p: Crucial talks between British and U.S. officials on negotiating a new "open skies" agreement due to start Monday in Washington have been delayed for two weeks due to a senior negotiator falling ill, a British government spokesman told Reuters.
"Our lead official is in hospital so the meeting has been cancelled. The talks have been postponed for a fortnight," he said.
The talks were scheduled to last three days as the two sides try to clinch a deal on liberalisation of the transatlantic airline market.
An open skies deal is a precondition for clearance of an alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines.
Separately, BA and American as well as rival carriers opposed to the alliance will testify at European Commission hearings on Monday and Tuesday.
